description: User-approved provider intent (AGENTS.md: 'Capability governance — the user decides'). Membership changes in either direction are reserved to the user; edit this file only with explicit in-session user approval, in the same commit as the code change it authorizes.

liveSelectionNotes.mistral: Approved in-session 2026-07-26: the user asked for Mistral as a first-class provider with 'equal parity to other providers', chose the seat id/label ('mistral' → 'Mistral') and chose full parity in one pass. The seat is the Mistral Vibe CLI over ACP on the user's plan subscription. It is NOT the same identity as Pi's `mistral/<model>` BYOK upstream, which remains a separate provider reached through Pi and is unaffected by this entry — the two share a brand word and a hue, nothing else.
liveSelectionNotes.muse: Approved in-session 2026-08-10: the user chose full live-selectable parity with the other CLI seats — admission by the standard binary/credential probe (Meta Model API key + muse CLI login), explicitly NOT an AntiGravity-style consent wall. Muse Code carries no equivalent ToS risk: the Meta Model API standard tier is an ordinary paid API and does not train on prompts or completions. The seat is the Muse Code CLI (muse exec --json) on the user's own key. Admission is fail-closed (includeWhenUnknown: false, modelled on pi): binary resolvable AND a credential present, so an unresolved probe leaves Muse out of the strict picker snapshot rather than surfacing a seat that cannot run.
liveSelectionNotes.devin: Approved in-session 2026-09-01: the user chose Devin as a full live-selectable seat (11th live-selectable / 12th provider identity), modelled on the Mistral ACP archetype. The seat is the Devin CLI (`devin acp` over stdio) on the user's own paid seat; auth is env keys (WINDSURF_API_KEY canonical, DEVIN_API_KEY, lowercase windsurf_api_key) or the stored credentials file ~/.local/share/devin/credentials.toml, with an optional UI-configurable custom api_server_url endpoint. No AntiGravity-style consent wall — a paid CLI/API seat like Mistral/Muse. This membership edit lands in the same commit as the code it authorizes.

conditionalOfferNotes.antigravity: Approved as a product capability, and deliberately NOT live-selectable. AntiGravity is offered only behind its consent wall: the two-part opt-in (antigravityEnabled + antigravityOptInAcceptedAt, recording the user's acknowledgement of whole-Google-account ban risk and that third-party access is expressly prohibited by the Antigravity Additional Terms) plus a configured BYO gemini-api key or agy opt-in producing a non-empty model catalog. Its absence from liveSelectableProviderIds is the approved design, not drift — do not 'fix' it. Promotion would be a capability change reserved to the user AND would silently delete the wall: every gate reads isLiveSelectableProvider(p) || (p === 'antigravity' && <condition>), so making the left side true short-circuits the condition. 2026-09-03 third transport lane, explicit in-session user approval: Google's own published ACP server (registry id antigravity-acp 1.0.0, Google LLC, proprietary; agy_acp_server.par on macOS/Linux, agy_acp_server.exe on Windows, ACP JSON-RPC over stdio, Linux requires --uid=) is a switchable alternative to the legacy agy CLI via the antigravityUseAcp Settings switch (default off = legacy CLI; the existing format is preserved, not removed). The lane stays behind the SAME unchanged two-part opt-in — the switch alone never launches anything; spawn re-checks isAntigravityOptInEnabled and fails closed. Provenance is pin-on-first-install per the user's binding ruling: the RC01 registry entry publishes no sha256, so the first downloaded archive's hash is pinned in a sidecar outside the extract directory and every later launch verifies against that pin and refuses on mismatch — no hash is invented or hardcoded. Archive extraction shells out to platform tools (ditto / unzip / Expand-Archive) per the user's binding ruling — no new npm dependency. The Antigravity Additional Terms STILL contain the verbatim third-party-access prohibition as of 2026-09-03; this lane does not soften the consent-wall copy, adds no disclosure key, and changes no ban-risk acknowledgement. antigravity remains in conditionallyOfferedProviderIds — NOT promoted.
